meta.seo_title: Physiotherapy Clinic Google Ads Case Study | PPC Guru
meta.meta_description: How PPC Guru launched a Kitchener physiotherapy and wellness clinic on Google Ads to about 13 genuine phone and form leads a month at roughly $56 each in its first months.

headline: Launching a Physiotherapy Clinic to ~13 Google Ads Leads a Month
summary_line: PPC Guru launched Blockline Physiotherapy & Wellness on Google Ads with call and lead-form tracking in place, and the clinic's first full months produced about 13 genuine phone and form leads a month at roughly $56 each — with genuine enquiries counted separately from Google Business Profile map actions and booking-button clicks.
client_context: Blockline Physiotherapy & Wellness is a physiotherapy and wellness clinic serving patients in the Kitchener–Waterloo area of Ontario, Canada. The clinic provides hands-on physiotherapy and related wellness care, and depends on a steady flow of new-patient enquiries — phone calls and online contact requests from people searching for treatment nearby. Google Ads is the clinic's channel for reaching those high-intent local searchers, which makes clean measurement of calls and form submissions important from the very first month.
background: Blockline Physiotherapy & Wellness partnered with PPC Guru in spring 2026 to launch its Google Ads presence. As a fresh build, the priority was a focused local Search campaign paired with proper conversion tracking, so the clinic could see genuine phone and form enquiries rather than vanity map actions.
analysis: PPC Guru built the account around a single local Search campaign for Kitchener and set up call tracking (ads and website), lead-form conversions, and clear separation of genuine leads from Google Business Profile local actions. That separation matters: the raw account activity is dominated by directions, website visits and booking-button clicks, so counting only real calls and forms keeps the numbers honest from day one.
analysis_points: Launch a single, focused local Search campaign targeting Kitchener–Waterloo.
Set up call tracking for both ad calls and website calls to the clinic line.
Add lead-form conversions for online contact requests.
Separate genuine calls and forms from Google Business Profile local actions and booking-button clicks so reporting reflects real enquiries.

timeline.what: PPC Guru launch — local Search campaign live with call and lead-form tracking; first full month delivered about 12 genuine leads.
About 14 genuine leads at roughly $53 each as targeting settled — the clinic's strongest month so far.
Current in-progress month at time of reporting; genuine-lead totals still finalizing as call and offline imports settle.

challenge: As a brand-new Google Ads account, the clinic had no history to build on and had to establish genuine local demand from a standing start. A further challenge was measurement clarity: most of the account's recorded activity is Google Business Profile map actions and booking-button clicks, which can badly overstate results if counted as leads. Isolating true phone and form enquiries was essential to report honestly and to steer bidding correctly.

changes.why: Concentrated budget on high-intent physiotherapy searches in Kitchener–Waterloo.
Captured phone enquiries — the primary way patients reach a clinic — as measurable conversions.
Tracked online contact requests alongside calls.
Excluded map directions, website visits and booking-button clicks so reporting reflects real enquiries, not vanity actions.
Let bidding optimize toward genuine calls and forms as early data accumulated.

technical.label: Lead signals
technical.value: Ad calls · Website calls · Lead forms

benchmark: Figures cover the clinic's first three months on Google Ads, so this is an early launch snapshot rather than a long-run trend. Genuine leads count only real phone calls and form submissions — the account's map actions and booking-button clicks (which run far higher) are excluded.
gradual: In its first full month (May 2026) the account produced about 12 genuine leads, then grew to about 14 in June at a lower cost per lead as targeting settled — a healthy early trajectory for a brand-new clinic account. July is the current in-progress month, with genuine-lead totals still finalizing as call and offline imports settle, so the story is best confirmed once the next full quarter completes.
lessons: Count real calls and form submissions — not map directions or booking-button clicks — so early results are honest.
Set up call tracking before launch; in a clinic, most enquiries come by phone.
Start with one focused local Search campaign to concentrate budget and data.
Give a new account a full quarter before drawing firm conclusions.
Keep the search terms clean early so budget reaches treatment-intent searches.
why_it_worked: Call and lead-form tracking was in place from the first day of spend.
Budget was concentrated on high-intent local physiotherapy searches.
Genuine leads were separated from vanity map actions, keeping reporting honest.
Early cost per lead improved as targeting settled.
outcome: In its opening months on Google Ads, Blockline Physiotherapy & Wellness is generating about 13 genuine phone and form enquiries a month at roughly $56 each, with a strong early conversion rate and clean measurement that separates real leads from map actions. This is an early launch snapshot on a young account; PPC Guru's recommended next step is to let the account complete a full quarter and re-confirm the trend before scaling budget.
cta: PPC Guru helps Canadian clinics launch on Google Ads with honest call-and-form tracking and focused local Search.
methodology: All figures are pulled directly from the client's Google Ads account and shown on a monthly basis. 'Genuine leads' are phone calls and lead-form submissions only; Google Business Profile local actions and booking-button clicks are excluded. The account has only three months of history (May–Jul 2026), so this is an early launch snapshot and July is treated as still settling.
lead_quality: Almost all genuine leads in the opening months are direct phone calls to the clinic's Kitchener line — the highest-intent enquiry type for physiotherapy.
